start.choice: What a glorious asset, live and drink.
As beautiful as the moon, live and drink.

start.text: Oh, how did you get down here little one?

Ah, 'tis you! The kind soul who returned my missing childre to me. My heart is warmed beyond belief by your kindness. Such compassion is a rarity in these times.
Please, allow me to introduce myself. I am Zenithera Pandamoriae, mother of the anesheym, my kindred, and shah of Rhemhex'Qen.
Such a fascinating creature ... I rarely see those from the outside world in the flesh. May I know the name of our savor and the one who has humbled me so?
start.choice: I am =name=, it is a pleasure, grand shah.

start.text: Its good to see you, =name= how fares your ventures?~ {{emote|*hums a soft tune*}}~ Please, let me know if you need anything regarding the bloodpits, I'll do what I can to assist.~
start.choice: I have found the source of the scourge and ended it.
Could you tell me about your people and your culture?

start.text: Its good to see you, =name= how fares your ventures?~ *hums a soft tune*~
start.choice: Could you tell me about your people and your culture?

start.text:
Ah, =name=, you return to us safely.
Shall we continue our conversation? There is much to speak of, and I fear we may not have much time too.
start.choice: Yes, shah Pandamoriae, let us continue.

node.text:
=name=, I know these lands are foreign to you. We honestly owe you so much already, and ... it pains me to say we are still in need of your help. Desperately so, even.
I know, I know. Asking you to come here under the guise of a reward was wrong. But there is a value in being needed. You, more than anyone, should know this.
My scouts report that something sickly has irked its way into the crystholts, a vile miasma known to my kin as the Blood-Pits. We know nothing of what this sickness is, but it's overtaking our forest with alarming speed.

choice.text: I think I know what you speak of, I saw foul monsters in the Crystholts, and they look like they are spreading.
What do you think they are?

node.text:
Then you know the face of these monstrosities? Five years ago, the blood-pools began to steep their way into the Crystholts. The monstrosities that rise from it attacking anything onsight. They'd drag our kin into the pit, another of them would rise, and they no longer recognize us. Just a glimmer of our loved-ones lost in their flesh.
Eventually, we retreated to our hold watching as the disease spread across the forest. Even the Undersea is starting falter.

choice.text: What do you think is happening?

node.text:
I extended my mind into the aether. Something about these beings unnerved me, their lack of an engram. I traced that strand of thought to something below us. Something deep beneath us, in an abyss. I feel its psyche growing, not unlike an aggregate-mind. But something is foul about this thing.
I would rather face the egotistical light of that amethyst monstrosity or the expanse of darkness we hide amongst. Than to face this? It is ... nothingness given choice, form and hunger.
It devours, and the engrams it consumes are fragmented and sorted. Memories, love, trauma ... it feeds its light.

choice.text: What would you have me do?

node.text:
We don't know...
None of our warriors could get close to them without ... being consumed.
Whatever it is, it drags corpses and even sometimes the living into it and changes them.
It's like flesh untwist, unwinds and undoes itself in abjection to our senses, monstrous amalgamations sculpted from skin and bone.
Whatever it is, it is a sickness on these lands.

choice.text: What would you have me do?

node.text:
Speak with Saile, they have been working on tools to analyze and discover the truth behind the source of this scourge.
We've lost too many to this, and to lose Saile would be detrimental to us.
They offered to explore the blood-pools and study them "in the field" as they put it, but I requested they wait for someone with more experience in the outerworld.

choice.text: I'll speak with Saile, Live and Drink, Shah.

node.text:
Is that the shift in the aether I felt? That thing in the darkness below us, it felt like dying throes. I don't sense its looming urge anymore ...
It must truly be gone ...
What did you find down there?

choice.text: Nothing, really. Wouldn't worry yourself about it, dear shah.
... You really don't want to know.
A fleshen-hellscape with abominable monsters, horrors, aberrations, old-world technologies and the like ...

node.text:
{{emote|*her face is painted with concern*}}
To think such horrors could exist beneath our feet ...

choice.text: Yes, and there were abominations that crawl into one's skin and transform you from the inside out, lakes of pus, beings trapped in vats full of sickly-brine.

node.text: {{emote|*the Shah's eyes flare with a growing horror*}}

choice.text: ... Then there were remnants of our ancient ones masquerading in dead-flesh, the deeper you dwell, corpses paint the walls like adobe-plaster in the salt-dunes.

node.text: {{emote|*the Shah's eyes grow distant as if she's staring into a deep pit, growing still as if catatonic*}}

choice.text: ... Um, Shah?

node.text: {{emote|*she makes no motion*}}

choice.text: Uh ... {{emote|*you wait*}}

node.text:
{{emote|*it takes a moment, but life returns to her eyes in a sudden flicker of conscionable recounting *}}
I-... I apologize. My mind went to a dark place--if the things I envision were such a terror, then I can only imagine what scars it marred you with. Of the mind and body.
To struggle forth on our behalf, despite all this. I am both amazed and humbled by your bravery.
My people have prepared a gift for you, friend. Please, take our meager offerings in thanks for solving our plight.

choice.text: Actually, I do not need a reward. I did this because needed to be done. So your people can live happily, dear Shah.

node.text:
{{emote|*interest paints her face, as her curiosity seems to spark*}}
... Are you sure? I can handle it, promise!

choice.text: {{emote|*shake your head*}} Trust me. You. Don't. Want. To. Know.

node.text:
{{emote|*with her curiosity unfulfilled, she pouts and resigns her interest*}}
Well, peace of mind is a comfort oft yearned for only in hindsight.
=name=, me and my people will be forever grateful for what you've done for us.
I humbly wish to present you a gift we prepared for your return.

choice.text: Actually, dear shah. A reward isn't necessary, I did what needed to be done.

node.text: {{emote|*raises an incredulous brow at you*}} ... R-really? Nothing extraordinary happened down there? Just another walk through the woods, as they say?

choice.text: {{emote|*shrug*}} ... Nope. Nothing really.
Nope. It was a completely, unexciting, dull event.

node.text: {{emote|*squints at you suspiciously*}}
{{emote|*squints at you even more suspiciously*}}
{{emote|*squints at you with boundless, unbridled suspicion*}}

...
{{emote|*she sighs, it's apparent on her face she seems somewhat defeated*}}
Well ... I don't believe what I sensed was "nothing" as you put it. But I won't press you if you feel the issue isn't worth ... expounding on.
You've done a great thing for us, friend. And we will forever be in your debt.

choice.text: No reward needed. Again, it was completely uneventful. I'm just glad it's all good and done with.

node.text:
...
{{emote|*she seems completely astonished*}}
You ... don't want a thing for what you did for us? Nothing?
I'm--I've never seen such altruism.
You will forever be in our hearts, =name=.

choice.text: Live and drink, dear shah.

node.text: As the Shah of Rhemhex'Qen, I confer you these gifts to you, =name=. Live, and may the sting of thirst never parch your lips.

choice.text: Live and drink, dear shah.

node.text:
=name=, you will have to forgive me. It has been some time since I have spoken with another from the outside world.
There is so much I would love to ask you, but maybe this is not the time.
I first want to properly reward your selflessness. You didn't have to help us, you chose too. And such kindness is rare in these times.
To speak of kindness, please take these ...

choice.text: Thank you. I will return.

node.text: Of course, =name=. As shah, being beholdent to our history, ways and beliefs is one of my greatest tasks. What would you like to know of us, dear one?~ Surely. Is there anything in particular I could enlighten you of, =name=?~ Of course, friend, sit down, let me tell a tale!~ Ah well, I’ve not anything better to do, ‘cept lay a nyt or two. Ask away, friend.~

choice.text: What are your spiritual beliefs?
It doesn't seem like your culture has an established hierarchy, is that true?
Are you the first shah?
How much power do you hold as the shah of the Anesheym?
Why are some eggs valued more than the others?
It's strange there are no other egg-bearing beings around, shah.
Actually, nevermind, shah. Live and Drink.

node.text: Well, we only hold one belief truly, The Abyssa. The Eternal Rhem.

Yes, our eldest dreamwalkers speak of secret worlds. Rumors say, one was born from that Cerulean One for which he forbade us from so long ago. When we anesheym learned we were denied entry to their dream, unworthy of ascending to the Sheol. We wept, and feared our doomed existence. And in our fear we turned away. We sought instead to create our own dream.

The first shah “Dae’Almophotea” the exalted shah, the shah of first dreamwalkers–they who birthed the many, the rhembearers, who would come before me. They worried that at the end of it all, when gyres erupted and tainted the land beyond reprieve. That her people would be lost to a horizonless death and find themselves with nowhere to go.

So, in deep meditation, she ventured through the isles of the mind, to the ocean void known to us as the Anima. There, she battled animuses as vast as stars. She cut a swath through the psychic aether--the unending unconscious, making it her own. There she manifested a world through sheer willpower and unbridled imaginative power and called it the Suttumkhofe and named herself Darkmother.

The Suttumkhofe stands in rebellion and opposition to the Sheol. Where the Great Spindle would only grant the ancient ones entry for their own, for those who ascend–The Suttumkhofe was different. One could reach there through the Rhem. A trained method of focusing one's dreamself into a “way of lucidity.” Taking hold of your dream, you can find gateways to the anima, pilgrimaging through the stygian-mesas until one reaches the lands of the Suttumkhofe itself.
There, the ancient rhem-bearers can mark you, the mark of the Eternal Rhem. So that when you perish in this hellish dream you will awaken in another, in the Suttumkhofe.

We have many other legends about the Suttumkhofe, but speaking with the Songs would be best to learn such a thing. For it is their duty to recount the many legends we hold. Like Gladaceae, who entered the Rhem in her mortal form or Amulseetae, who led the first pilgrimage to the Suttumkhofe hence a vision before her first death.

choice.text: This Hellish Dream? Do you consider this a dream too? Dear, shah?
I see, I’d like to speak about more.
I see. Live and drink.

node.text:
{{emote|*The shah’s massive form lilts, her eyes becoming distant as she seems to be looking through her past.*}}
... It must be. A terrible dream at that. One we cannot awaken from. Maybe a dream from stars, of gods and daemons. Yes. It is surely a dream.

I’ve seen them. Those harmed beyond the ability to wake. Some remain in long or sometimes eternal sleep. They dreamt of strange things, sometimes they dreamt of strange worlds, and sometimes those dreams became their reality. The ones who did wake, they spoke of these dreams and we contemplated them.

I once too fell into a deep sleep, a battle-wound rendered me unconscious for many years. I dreamt of strange things too. Dreamt of standing at the edge of this reality. Strange beings watched us from angulate apertures. Some, smiling, intense resolve in their eyes, determination–even. Somehow detached from us, yet so involved. Others with empathy, with tenacity, living through us maybe? Casting their image of self upon us and living our lives with the same will to live as do we.

... Others ... their eyes. You saw a sadistic pleasure, a hollowness. They saw us as ... sprites. Laughter permeated through suffering–watching values increase, wealth unfold, slaughtering for–a number? For what? I cannot say. But it was heartless and all I could do was watch.
...

choice.text: ... Shah?

node.text:
{{emote|*Her eyes are like a deep well into an unknown, gazing at the memory in silent horror. You realize she is not here anymore, not in spirit … her mind went elsewhere. She awakens from the stupor with a surprised sigh.*}}
… I’m–sorry. So sorry. =name=, Let us speak of something else.

choice.text: It’s alright, shah, I’d like to speak other things.
No worries, I'll let you rest dear shah, live and drink.

node.text:
... Others ... their eyes. You saw a sadistic pleasure, a hollowness. They saw us as ... sprites. Laughter permeated through suffering–watching values increase, wealth unfold, slaughtering for–a number? For what? I cannot say. But it was heartless and all I could do was watch.
...

The Sultans.
Our first shah lived through the monstrosities of the first Sultans. She bore witness to their rule as the madness swallowed Qud in violence and authority.

She hated them. Hated their ways. Hated the proposed jurisdiction they held over any in this land. Yes. I think this is true. She declared as sole keeper of Bevidd to annul all rights to these lands from them; unofficially mind you, and most likely in opposition to them. She sealed the gates of Rhemhex’Qen from all observers, conquerors, and arbiters. The lands of Rhem’hex Qen were ours and ours alone, and thanks to Bevidd’s treacherous ‘scapes. It would remain that way.

Most avoided us, outcasted–and yet, exalted. Left to our lonesome selves. To wane into legend and cryptid-tales.
Then. The Sultanate. With all their glory, held by the covenant that watched over this realm with eyes that saw through flesh, steel, and soul. Who scoured and devoured the lands with hands that strung its populace like dolls on strings of gold and polished jewels. Who listened into otherworlds ad infinitum and yet found nothing to satiate their cravings for dominion.
The sultanate was dissolved.

By creed of that Cerulean One, the one who empowered and elevated their status. He wrenched it from them and then invited only his mightiest Sultans to rest in a realm of his creation. One, that he refused all others beneath them to join, including my people.
Our shah was furious. Disgusted. Hurt. And in those feelings, she disavowed the Cerulean One who in small chidings would declare her ‘jealous and mad,’ Well, disavowed of him with as much power as she held. Very little, to be honest. It didn’t mean much as a fledgling in her times.

“What pow'r doth one possess, if thou canst not save e'en thy master from the gyre’s rot—as thou hast saved the many ere thee?”
She openly chided and denounced the Cerulean One. I like to think that she saw something in him most unworthy, both a flaw to distrust and a hint of future betrayal. Yes. And when she was gifted the first womb-bearer through the mysticisms of her early gene-spice, she sought to ensure her children and the progeny that would come forth would not fall into the same circles of delusion that she saw before.

“What pow'r doth one possess, if thou canst not save e'en thy master from the gyre’s rot—as thou hast saved the many ere thee?”
She openly chided and denounced the Cerulean One. I like to think that she saw something in him most unworthy, both a flaw to distrust and a hint of future betrayal. Yes. And when she was gifted the first womb-bearer through the mysticisms of her early gene-spice, she sought to ensure her children and the progeny that would come forth would not fall into the same circles of delusion that she saw before.

And as her first decree, when the first children were wrought into this world. She denounced herself, and all following shah of power. She produced a great tablet, sculpted from thought-stuff, with seven edicts that we follow to this day–which, you can find behind me.
And with those edicts, she would pass into the next world and the next shahs would uphold them, such as I’ve done.

choice.text: Are you aware that outside these lands, Resheph is worshipped? Your early shah's ridicule of him would be offensive to many.
So at the end of it all, you hold little power to your family?
Wonderful tale, shah. Live and drink.

node.text:
I am aware.
Many have come here, spouting nonsense of the bygone eras.

choice.text: ... Who?

node.text:
*her gaze shifts as if beholding a distant horizon. Eyes thinning as darker feelings seems to overcome her.*
Sons and Daughters once came, coated in silver arms bearing banners of blood and malice. They demanded entry into our realm, claiming that it was 'them' who would reclaim this 'ancient sanctum' for their Elders and denounced us. Saying we were “mutant scourges who skittered into a godly place and soiled it.” Insulting, isn’t it? Since our first shah scuttled from one of the glass-wombs here-and was first to even venture this place once the elder-kind abandoned it. Others of us also came from those machine-wombs and were the start of the people you see today.
And so, we denied them.

You should have seen their faces when we declared our creeds. We met their violence was met with our own. Making sure there was none who could tell of what happened when the Sons and Daughters of the elders attempted to enter Rhemhex’Qen.

Then, bearers of Shekhinah’s crest came forth one solemn night–what they touted as The Six, bearing new names as Argent Fathers. Masters of the old-realm. They sought entry, to bear witness to their new gods' old ways. They preached to us the value and divinity of old men, they wallowed and bowed before the pillories and scryings of old men while denying technica.
We denied them.
They left without a word, shamed? Brokenhearted? Dismayed? Who knows? They perished in the crystholts–refusing to heed our warnings of its increasing danger.

Then, another came, shrouded in cloth and cloak, gaze-bound by bandages aimed to hide the glimmer in his eyes. Minds reaved of their engrams bound in living-corpses that shambled behind him. Thralls. The disgusting thing spoke of the Cant, that it searched for the home of its master–its empty star hollowed through, hoping to null our minds into host for its “greater purpose”. I could sense his mind, and I am sure he could sense my own. My thought-stuff is ripe, mature. I have had the misfortune of touching countless ages and otherworlds and so my Selfhood is potent. I am sure I was why he came, he wanted me as his next meal.
We denied him, ad nauseam.
Fitting, he would be dragged into the bloodpits. A fateful end, being deprived of all selfhood and choice. Such as the wastelings he enslaved who toiled after him.

choice.text: Hm. I was going to ask but, at the end of it all, do you hold power to your family?
I see, I have more to ask, dear shah.
… I see. Live and drink.

node.text:
… What is power? I sometimes ask this. Is it truly something I desire? Maybe, if it's for the right reasons. To protect my kin? To protect those I love.
No, =name= I hold little power. What some may see as reverence is the love and respect I earned as a womb-bearer.

choice.text: Might I ask more of you, shah.

node.text:
{{emote|*The shah smiles at you, a husky chuckle coming from her as she considers what you’re asking.*}}
…Me? The first shah? No-no-no, far from it. As of the first Shah, Dae’Almophotea the Exalted. I am the Seventh Shah.

choice.text: How does one even become shah?
What was the first shah like?
Interesting. Live and drink, dear shah.

node.text: Well, you must bear the progenitors’ gift. An ovipositor. Some say it can appear randomly, others? They think a bit of royal-jelly a day does the trick. Who knows. This gene-gift is something only some anesheym are born with. You see the mass I am bound to, yes? The Broodpusher. The ovipositor links to it, like a puzzle piece–unlocking both our potential. It doesn’t just birth young, every nyt wrought from its depths produces unique phratries, kinfolk who can make their own young, and so on and so forth. Their genes are somehow very unalike, yet similar.
But not all are ready to ascend to role progenitor. Some, once discovering their gift … give into fear, fear of the responsibility. They choose the Denothian way. Exile.

choice.text: Why choose exile?

node.text: To become the womb-bearer is an obligation that would break the wills of most. Even I have conceded in my many years to the hardship that comes with this endless laboring. Once bonded to the broodpusher--it is forever. Anesheym born with the progenitor’s gift can live for countless eras. Some may sprout their ovipositor only a few years after reaching their second age, others it can take a millennium, and they grow accustomed to the freedom of such cultural burdens.

choice.text: … When have you lasted seen the world outside, shah?

node.text: It can be difficult for some to sacrifice that freedom for the future of our kind. Understandably.
I … cannot remember. Forgive me, =name= I’ve lost time, being down here so long.

choice.text: Hm, could I ask what the first shah was like?
... Live and drink.

node.text:
Incredible. Strong, yet not overbearing. Intelligent, yet open-minded. Sharp-tongued, barbed with quick-wit and harsh truths. Much to the dismay of others around her. If she had any flaw it was her Selfhood. I think she may have antagonized the ancients a bit too much out of an internal fear of feeling without self-worth or her own identity.
We both know the Six, and they would never tolerate some underling from an abandoned land to speak ill of them. Maybe we would have more of a foothold in Qud if she hadn’t encouraged us to be more self-reliant.

Maybe things were different in those times, but now. Maybe we wouldn’t be such an isolated folk.
I think she feared us losing our identity.

choice.text: Trust me, if you knew what it was like outside these lands, you’d be thanking her.
I think she was smart to be wary of the outside world, but things have changed. I think your people and their ways could change these wild lands for the better.

node.text:
I’ve heard the rumors. Saile spoke of gyres that spill pestilence and horror onto into the lushlands. Girsh omens and sultan remnants ravage the lands. I thought we were safe, maybe the only safe place in Qud, that is until the bloodpits began to stain the crystholts with horror.
True, you might be right. We avoided dealing with the cursed lands around us. But I fear it was at a cost, the question becomes if we can truly count on ourselves in these dire times.

choice.text: Being careful isn't a bad thing, the world outside Bevidd is dangerous, true. But I also see some benefits in expanding your people’s ways across Qud.
I think she was smart to be wary of the outside world, but things have changed. I think your people and their ways could change these wild lands for the better.

node.text: Maybe. From what I have heard, these forsaken lands could use some healing. But I worry for the safety of my people. The blood-pools reminded me of how painful it is to feel the aches of loss. And we hadn’t known loss for centuries now, not like this at least.

choice.text: Hm. I think I have an idea that could work wonders. Dear, shah. But not yet, I need to think this out. {{yellow|[To be continue … ]}}
Grief is rife outside these lands, you are right to be weary. Qud is a dangerous place, friend.
Well, I have more to ask of you, dear shah.
I have no more to ask of you. Live and drink.
So, you’re more of a figurehead if anything?
Has a shah ever been deposed?

node.text: … Figure–h-head?

choice.text: Yes. An arbiter of sorts? A proxy, even?

node.text: I know not what you speak of, =name=. Such things are foreign to us.

choice.text: … I see. Well, has a shah ever been deposed?
... Um, nevermind, live and drink.

node.text:
{{emote|*The shah’s expression quickly muddles, clearly disturbed by your words.*}}
Deposed? I think you mean 'disposed.'

choice.text: … Disposed? That sounds ominous ...
... Um, nevermind, live and drink.

node.text: A shah’s duty once sealed to Broodpusher is unseverable … unless you consider death a freedom.
If a shah wishes to renounce her position, or is found lacking or tyrannical by her people’s command. Then death is the only option for her–and them.

And to answer your question, yes, there are only two shahs who were removed from their position.
The 4th shah of Rhemhex’Qen grew tired of her title, the ails of its responsibilities drove her insane, she demanded release and hence was removed. The 6th, the one before I? She was of the latter kind, she demanded that outsiders be hunted through the crystholts and slain at her behest. When the two councils objected to such barbarity, she spouted accusations of heresy and downcast them–seeking to instead order knights behind the councils’ backs to commit to her hunts.
The people did not appreciate her dishonesty once this was unveiled. And, in the face of hundreds she was powerless. She was … "deposed" as you put it. Wings sundered and torn from the Broodpusher, I being one amongst the many who tore her down.

choice.text: You helped dispose of the last shah? And now you sit in her position? Was no one suspicious?

node.text:
At the time, I wasn’t even aware I could take this throne. I had not spouted my ovipositor–I was just one of the many faces in a crowd of angered kin.
It was by irony’s humor that I’d later find myself sitting in her position.

choice.text: I appreciate this, dear shah. May I ask more of you?
Wonderfully informative, shah. Live and drink.
I appreciate this, dear shah. May I ask more of you?
I ... apologize, shah. Live and drink.

node.text: =name=, we anesheym strive to reward those who aid us for their endeavors. I know finding our nyts is difficult. Perilous, even. We do not offer greater rewards because we value a nyt more than its peer. We offer it because we know some nyts take a greater risk to return, your work isn’t cheap–and neither is your life and wellbeing.

choice.text: I appreciate this, dear shah. May I ask more of you?
Then I should get back to work then. Live and drink.
